resources.string: Check the text before you tap
Read how Veritxt handles your information before you start.
The SMS text you paste, share, or allow it to receive. For incoming SMS, the sender’s number is held temporarily so you can review and choose whether to block it. Sender identity is not verified.
On this phone only. Veritxt has no internet permission, so your messages are never sent anywhere.

Message text and sender numbers are not saved to app storage. Incoming reports show the numeric sender and a short message preview in unlocked notifications. Those reports are hidden on the lock screen; the group header shows only a count. Android notification history and notification-access apps may retain displayed previews. Pending checks expire after 10 minutes; leaving the app clears the current scan. Veritxt saves only your settings and notice acceptance. Copying a sender’s number uses Android’s clipboard only when you choose.
You can check messages by pasting or sharing them. Reading new SMS needs your permission, and you can turn it off anytime.

Under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173), you have the right to be informed, to object, to access, and to have your data corrected or erased. Because Veritxt stores no messages, only the settings on your phone can be accessed or erased.

Only your privacy-notice agreement, onboarding, incoming-SMS choice, and display and language settings are saved. No scan history or raw messages are kept. The app has no internet permission.
Android treats SMS access as a restricted permission and may refuse it. Force-stopping the app pauses incoming checks until you open it again.

With your consent, supported builds assess new SMS on this phone. Each unlocked notification shows the numeric sender, a short message preview, risk level and gauge. Expand for the score, model category and initial analysis. An unavailable scan has no score. Reports are grouped together, with one report per SMS. Sender and preview are hidden on the lock screen. Android notification history and notification-access apps may retain previews. Pending messages expire after 10 minutes and are not saved to app storage. View report opens the exact message. Veritxt does not read your inbox or change messages. Android may restrict SMS access. Notifications need separate permission.
SMS permission granted. Veritxt will check new texts as they arrive.
SMS permission was not granted. You can still paste or share messages, or allow it later in Android settings.
This clears your privacy agreement, consent and display preferences, and current checking session. You\'ll see the privacy notice again. Android permissions remain under system settings.
Veritxt can only warn you about a new text if these are all OK. Fix anything marked below.
Not granted. Turn on “When a new SMS arrives” in Settings, or allow SMS in Android settings.
Off. Turn it on in Settings.
Blocked or muted. Allow notifications for Veritxt.
Android may stop Veritxt in the background. Set Veritxt to “Unrestricted” or “Don\'t optimize”.
Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Veritxt → turn on Autostart. Also set Battery saver to “No restrictions”.
Settings → Battery → App battery management (or More settings) → Veritxt → allow Background activity and Auto launch.
Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management → Veritxt → Allow. Also turn on Veritxt in i Manager → App manager → Autostart.
Settings → Battery → App launch → Veritxt → choose Manage manually and turn on Auto-launch and Run in background.
Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → make sure Veritxt is not in Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps.
Look for Autostart or Background activity in your battery settings and allow Veritxt.
If you force-stop Veritxt, Android won\'t deliver new texts to it until you open the app again.
On Android 13 and newer, apps installed from an APK may need extra approval: open App info → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then turn on SMS again.
Chat messages in Google Messages or Samsung Messages aren\'t SMS, so Veritxt never sees them. Copy and paste them instead.

New SMS are scanned automatically while incoming SMS is on. Grouped reports identify each sender and show a short preview, risk level and gauge while unlocked. Expand for the score and analysis. Results are experimental and may be incorrect. Reporting is disabled.
Automatic scanning is unavailable in this build. Incoming notifications show Unable to assess without a score. Open View report to try a manual check. Reporting is disabled.
Loading or checking is taking longer. You can clear or leave this screen.
Wait, then check again. If it remains stuck, close the app through Android settings and reopen it. No new check was started.
The SMS model assessed only the beginning; visible-text indicators cover the full submitted message.
Automatic warnings and reporting are disabled.

Risk scores are provisional evidence indices, not statistical probabilities: Low Risk 0–29, Medium Risk 30–69, High Risk 70–100. Repeated indicators count once. A model flag contributes 40 points; requests to send or share credentials 70; credential entry requests, payment requests, and obscured URL structures 30 each; urgency, reward language, and shortened URLs 10 each. Link presence and organization names alone add no points. The total is capped at 100. A low score does not establish authenticity. These weights and thresholds require representative validation.

Unable to assess has no numerical score. It applies when evidence or a usable model is unavailable, a check fails, or the input falls outside supported analysis. Phone numbers alone cannot establish fraud. Plain URLs and email addresses cannot establish reputation or identity. Email text is assessed only for visible patterns, without using the SMS model. No live domain reputation or email authentication check is available. Veritxt never blocks numbers automatically.
Provisional evidence index; not a probability of fraud.
No significant indicators of fraudulent activity were detected.
Potentially suspicious elements were identified. Further verification is recommended.
Strong indicators associated with phishing, smishing, or fraudulent activity were identified.
Insufficient information was available to determine a reliable risk classification.
No immediate action is required. Continue exercising caution when interacting with unfamiliar senders or links.
Verify the sender’s identity before responding, opening links, or sharing personal information. Consider blocking the number if the contact is unwanted.
Avoid interacting with the sender, opening suspicious links, or providing sensitive information. Consider blocking and reporting the number.
Verify the sender through an official channel or provide additional information for further analysis.
No significant indicators were identified by the available checks.
The available evidence does not support a reliable assessment.
Indicators suggest possible risk; they do not confirm fraud. Links and sender identities are not verified. No live threat intelligence is available.
Provide meaningful message text. Numbers, links alone, and unrecognized text may not provide sufficient evidence.
A phone number alone does not establish identity or fraudulent activity. This app has no phone reputation lookup.
Only the visible URL structure was checked. The destination was not opened and its reputation is unknown.
Only visible text patterns can be checked. Email ownership, headers, authentication, and sender identity are not verified; the SMS model is not used for email classification.
A request to send or share a password, PIN, OTP, or other sensitive credential was identified.
A request to enter or verify sensitive credentials was identified. It may be legitimate; verify the destination independently.
An organization name is mentioned. Its identity is unverified; the name alone adds no risk points.
A URL uses a numeric address, internationalized hostname, or embedded user information. These structures can obscure the destination and also occur on legitimate sites.
A request involving payment or a money transfer was identified. Verify it independently.
The SMS model flagged language patterns associated with suspicious messages. This is a supporting signal, not confirmation of fraud.
Time pressure or account restriction language was identified.
Prize or reward language was identified.
A shortened URL conceals the final destination.
A link is present. Link presence alone does not increase the risk score.

Copy the sender’s number if needed, then open Android’s blocked-number screen. Add or paste the number and confirm there. Check it against the conversation in Messages first. Veritxt cannot confirm whether it was blocked. Leaving Veritxt clears this scan.
Number supplied with the incoming SMS. Sender identity is not verified.
The sender’s number is unavailable for this scan. Check the original conversation in Messages; numbers in the message text may belong to someone else.

Open Android’s blocked-number screen, then add and confirm the sender’s number there. Verify the sender in your Messages or Phone app first; a number inside a message may belong to someone else. Veritxt does not select a number or confirm whether it was blocked. Leaving Veritxt clears this scan.
Android’s blocked-number screen could not be opened on this device or user profile. Use the steps below instead.

1. Open the conversation in Messages, or the caller in Phone → Recents.
2. Check the actual sender or caller number.
3. Open Details, Info, or the menu, then select Block number or Block and report spam.
4. Review the selected number and confirm there.

Menu names vary by device and app. For email, use your email app to block or report the sender. For a suspicious URL, report it through the impersonated service using an official channel. Veritxt cannot confirm whether a number was blocked.
The model predicts legitimate SMS, fraudulent SMS, or gambling advertising. The risk index below also considers visible warning signs.
The model predicts Ham or Smishing. The risk index below also considers visible warning signs.
The category with the largest model margin is selected. These margins are not probabilities or the risk index.
A cashback offer asks you to claim it before a deadline. Verify it independently through the bank’s app or official contact details.
A cashback or rebate claim with an expiry deadline and a link adds 30 points. A model flag adds 40 points; together they give High Risk at 70 points. A model flag alone stays Medium Risk.
